subject: english
chapter_title: A Triumph of Surgery: Tricki and Mrs Pumphrey

concepts.title: Mrs Pumphrey's Overindulgence of Tricki
concepts.definition: Mrs Pumphrey, a rich lady, pampers her dog Tricki with cream cakes, chocolates and rich food between meals, giving him no exercise, so the little dog becomes hugely fat and listless like a bloated sausage.
concepts.key_idea: Her worry about Tricki's listlessness is solved with wrong remedies, more malt and cod-liver oil and Horlicks, which deepen the illness.

what food does mrs pumphrey give to tricki

solution_steps.explain: Cream cakes, chocolates, rich meals, malt, cod-liver oil and Horlicks make up Tricki's routine.
No exercise follows the rich diet, so Tricki turns rheumatic and fat.
Mrs Pumphrey treats listlessness as weakness, while Herriot sees it as overfeeding.

concepts.title: Herriot's Treatment: No Food but Plenty of Play
concepts.definition: Mr Herriot takes Tricki to his surgery and treats him with no medicine at all: two days of only water, then plain food and vigorous play with the other dogs restore the animal's health through discipline and companionship.
concepts.key_idea: The cure lies in cutting off the rich diet and letting Tricki run and fight with the household dogs, which his mistress would never have allowed.

solution_steps.explain: No food for two days, only water, burns off the excess; then plain meals begin.
Tricki joins the other dogs, fights and runs, and his eyes brighten with new energy.
Herriot calls the recovery a triumph of surgery because no surgery or drugs were needed at all.

concepts.title: Eggs, Wine and Brandy: Tricki Gets Better
concepts.definition: Mrs Pumphrey showers the surgery with eggs, wine and brandy for Tricki's convalescence, and Mr Herriot and his partners enjoy the luxuries themselves, while Tricki, delighted, takes his mistress as a wonderful deal better than anyone.
concepts.key_idea: When Tricki returns as a lithe, hard-muscled animal, Mrs Pumphrey's tearful joy keeps her from ever learning that the treatment was simply no food and lots of play.

solution_steps.explain: Eggs, wine and brandy arrived daily, meant for Tricki but consumed by the household.
Tricki bounds out as a lithe, hard-muscled animal, springing into Mrs Pumphrey's arms.
The tearful mistress never learns the plain truth, which makes the story's triumph comic.

concepts.title: The Triumph of Surgery and Love of a Dog
concepts.definition: The story warns that overpampering harms the one you love: a pet needs discipline, exercise and simple food, and blind affection dressed as care only breeds sickness.
concepts.key_idea: Herriot's professional honesty versus Mrs Pumphrey's sentimentality carries the moral that real love acts wisely, not indulgently.

solution_steps.explain: Overindulgence without exercise and diet control breeds illness in pets.
Mrs Pumphrey's sentimental love clashes with Herriot's professional, disciplined care.

solution_steps.action: verify the irony of the title
solution_steps.explain: The triumph is of common sense, not surgery, since no operation or drug was used.
